how: We read the website of every Houston wedding florist listed on Lazo (266 listings, 202 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: bouquet preservation services, a silk-flower showroom, venues, and retail delivery shops with no wedding page. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: What holds up in Houston heat and humidity for an outdoor ceremony in my month, and what wilts?
Do you design for the venue, or deliver arrangements? Installation and teardown are the difference in price.
Can I see a full wedding's florals at a budget like mine, not just a bouquet photo?

picks.name: The Red Experience, llc
picks.blurb: The Red Experience is a Houston wedding florist and event designer in Pearland doing bespoke floral design, planned from first idea to final installation. The founder started in 2004 making handbags in graduate school before a friend's wedding turned her toward flowers.

picks.name: Bring Joy - Florals & Events
picks.blurb: Lauren started Bring Joy in 2017 on the side of a full-time job, went full time in 2022 and brought her sister Rebecca on in 2023. Simple, budget-friendly wedding flower packages you can browse as collections, for bouquets, boutonnieres, centerpieces and cake flowers.

picks.name: Dream Bouquet
picks.blurb: Rebekah began designing in 1991 and founded Dream Bouquet in 1996, growing it from an in-home business into a Houston wedding and event floral company. Wedding florals remain the heart of it, across Greater Houston and Texas from the Gulf Coast to the Hill Country.

picks.name: Floral Events
picks.blurb: Floral Events has designed custom wedding and event florals in Houston since 1995, from backyard weddings to the Super Bowl and the Houston Rodeo. Still locally owned, and a preferred vendor at The Bell Tower on 34th, The Astorian and NRG Park.

picks.name: Casa De Flores Floral Design
picks.blurb: Mariela learned floral design helping her mother Teofila at a small flower tent in Brookshire, then trained formally and graduated from Texas A&M. Casa De Flores is the family's West Houston studio, seen on HBO Max's Full Bloom, doing weddings alongside delivery.

picks.name: Isi Floral Design & Event Decor
picks.blurb: Isi Floral Design in Spring sells wedding florals and event decor as packages, each with custom florals, decor, tableware and personal touches, sized to the guest count. Weddings and celebrations across Houston and Texas.

picks.name: Whimsical Creative
picks.blurb: Whimsical Creative does floral design and wedding planning from the same Houston team, so the flowers are designed with the whole room in mind. Florals can be booked on their own or with coordination, for a relaxed, high-end feel.

picks.name: Lush Flowers
picks.blurb: Rene' Johnson has worked in weddings and events for over 30 years and was lead floral designer for David Tutera on multiple weddings. Lush Flowers is her Houston shop, with same-day delivery alongside the wedding work.

picks.name: Mibellarosa
picks.blurb: Mibellarosa's motto is more is more: full, lush, opulent florals in a style it calls Modern Impressionism, featured by HBO Max, Good Morning America and Martha Stewart Weddings. A Houston boutique for destination weddings and couples who want fashion in the flowers.

picks.name: Secret Floral Garden
picks.blurb: Linda started Secret Floral Garden in her garage in 2002 with her baby son strapped to her chest, and it has grown into a full floral and event design company. Flowers plus lounge furniture, bars, linens, chairs and other rentals from one Houston team.

picks.name: Lily in June
picks.blurb: Lily in June does wedding planning and floral design together, with a team drawn from hospitality, design, logistics and event production. Based in Navasota, working Houston, College Station, Dallas and nearby.

picks.name: Window Box Florist (prev. Mainland Floral)
picks.blurb: The traditional shop option: Window Box Florist is the former Mainland Floral, on Galveston Island since 1935 and renamed in 2024 with the same owners and staff. Custom wedding designs from intimate to grand, with shops in Galveston and Pearland.
